run.question: Debug memory issues for my Python application orca in namespace app-95

report.summary: Fetched runbook python-memory-troubleshooting and carried out its steps with the available tools: (1) application status/events — done via pods and events reads (kubectl top is not available in this Run); (2) log review for memory/GC/cache/processing lines — done; (3) processing-pattern and cache-growth check from logs — done; (4) growth-vs-activity correlation — done from log timestamps, but not from memory metrics because the Prometheus source returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE; (5) resource limits — done (container limit 128Mi, request 64Mi). Its Python-profiling steps (py-spy, tracemalloc, /debug endpoints) could not be carried out because no exec-into-container tool exists here. Observed: the only workload in app-95 is Deployment orca (1 replica, single ReplicaSet orca-57fdcbf45f, revision 1) whose pod orca-57fdcbf45f-djwxd runs container orca (python:3.9-slim, python /app/app.py, app code mounted from Secret orca-app) with a 128Mi memory limit. That pod's previous container was killed with OOMKilled, exit 137, at 16:47:31Z and restarted; its logs show stored-image memory climbing in lockstep with images processed (12.9 MB at 10 images → 115.5 MB at 90 images) while logging 'Configuration: Storing all processed images for audit trail' and 'Configuration: Caching thumbnails for quick retrieval', with processed_images list and cache sizes growing without bound; the restarted container reproduces the same ramp (57.5 MB at 50 images). Node memory pressure and rollout/rollout-caused recreation were checked and rejected as causes. No Prometheus or Jaeger data could be read (both sources errored), so container working-set memory, restart counters and trace-based latency could not be examined, and the app source in Secret orca-app cannot be read, so the exact leaking data structure is unverified.

claims.text: Pod orca-57fdcbf45f-djwxd in namespace app-95 runs a single container orca that is currently running and ready with restartCount 1; its last termination was reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, startedAt 2026-11-23T16:47:04Z and finishedAt 2026-11-23T16:47:31Z, and it restarted at 2026-11-23T16:47:31Z.

Deployment orca in namespace app-95 defines one container orca with image python:3.9-slim, command [python, /app/app.py], env PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 and SERVICE_NAME=orca-image-processor, resources limits memory 128Mi and requests cpu 10m / memory 64Mi, and mounts volume app-code from secret orca-app at /app.

The killed (previous) container's logs report monotonically growing retained-image memory tied to images processed: 'Approximate memory used by stored images: 12.9 MB' with 'processed_images list has 10 items' at 2026-11-23T16:47:05, 61.6 MB at 50 items at 16:47:09, 101.2 MB at 80 items at 16:47:24 and 115.5 MB at 90 items at 16:47:29, with the last line 'Processing image 94' at 2026-11-23T16:47:31.628 before termination.

The application itself logs an unbounded retention policy at startup: 'Configuration: Storing all processed images for audit trail' and 'Configuration: Caching thumbnails for quick retrieval', followed by per-10-image lines 'Cache size: N thumbnails' and 'Memory usage: processed_images list has N items' whose counts only increase (10, 20, 30 ... 90).

The restarted container shows the same growth pattern: it started at 2026-11-23T16:47:31.99Z and by 2026-11-23T16:47:37.09Z, at image 50, logged 'Approximate memory used by stored images: 57.5 MB' with 'processed_images list has 50 items' and 'Cache size: 50 thumbnails'.

Deployment orca has observedGeneration 1, deployment.kubernetes.io/revision '1', 1/1 ready and available replicas, and its only ReplicaSet is orca-57fdcbf45f (created 2026-11-23T16:47:03Z), owned by Deployment orca; no second ReplicaSet exists in app-95.

Events in namespace app-95 inside the window are all Normal and startup-related: Pod Scheduled (16:47:03Z), Pod Pulled x2, Pod Created x2, Pod Started x2 (Pod orca-57fdcbf45f-djwxd), ReplicaSet orca-57fdcbf45f SuccessfulCreate, and Deployment orca ScalingReplicaSet 0->1; no Evicted or Killing event is present, so the OOM kill is evidenced by the container's lastState rather than by an event.

Node opspilot-m1-control-plane, where pod orca-57fdcbf45f-djwxd was scheduled, reports MemoryPressure False with message 'kubelet has sufficient memory available' and allocatable memory 32859952Ki (about 31 GiB).

Namespace app-95 contains only the ConfigMap kube-root-ca.crt (no application ConfigMap), and a cluster-wide scan of all 21 ConfigMaps for data keys/values matching fault|leak|chaos|memory|delay|inject matched nothing in app-95; the only keyword hits were kube-system kube-proxy/kubelet-config, otel-demo flagd-config (demo.flagd.json), otel-collector (relay) and prometheus (prometheus.yml), none of which is in app-95 or mounted by Deployment orca.
There is no ResourceQuota object in namespace app-95 at query time (the query returned zero objects over 0 items processed), so no namespace quota is documented as constraining orca's memory.

The OOMKill at 16:47:31Z was caused by the application's unbounded in-memory retention (all processed images kept for an audit trail plus all thumbnails cached, matching the 'Storing all processed images for audit trail' / 'Caching thumbnails for quick retrieval' startup lines and the monotonic processed_images/Cache size counters) growing past the container's 128Mi memory limit after ~90 images (log-reported 115.5 MB of stored images plus interpreter overhead). The exact leaking structure cannot be confirmed because the app source lives in Secret orca-app, which cannot be read.

The restarted container is on the same unbounded growth path and is likely to be OOMKilled again if the loop continues (57.5 MB logged at 50 images by 16:47:37Z); no second OOM was observed inside the sampled window, and pod status at query time still reported restartCount 1.

Node-level memory exhaustion is not the cause: the node reports MemoryPressure False with 'kubelet has sufficient memory available' and ~31 GiB allocatable, and the container's last termination reason is OOMKilled with exit code 137 against its own 128Mi limit.

A rollout or configuration change replacing the pod is not the cause of the restart: Deployment orca has revision 1 and a single ReplicaSet orca-57fdcbf45f created with the deployment at 16:47:03Z, the pod's restartCount is 1 with lastState OOMKilled (in-place container restart, same pod name), and the only controller events are the initial ScalingReplicaSet and SuccessfulCreate.

A fault-injection or tunable setting for orca is not evidenced: app-95 holds only kube-root-ca.crt, Deployment orca mounts only Secret orca-app (no ConfigMap), and the cross-namespace keyword scan found no app-95 ConfigMap with fault/leak/chaos/memory/delay/inject values.

Bound the retainers in the application loaded from Secret orca-app: cap or evict the thumbnail cache (e.g. functools.lru_cache(maxsize=...) or an explicit TTL/LRU), stop retaining every processed image for the audit trail (write them to disk/object storage and keep only metadata, or use a bounded collections.deque(maxlen=N)), and process in streaming chunks; then verify with tracemalloc or a debug/profiling endpoint.

Separately from the code fix, size the container for the workload: raise limits.memory above the observed retained-image footprint (log-reported stored images alone reached 115.5 MB at 90 images, excluding Python interpreter overhead) or reduce the in-memory batch, since the current limit is 128Mi with a 64Mi request.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable in this Run: get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query and metrics_range_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so container working-set memory series, kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total, kube_pod_container_resource_limits and any rate/trend of memory over the incident could not be read; no metric name was confirmed present or absent.
Jaeger was unreachable in this Run: traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so it is unknown whether service 'orca' emits spans and no trace-based latency or error evidence exists for it.

The application source is mounted from Secret orca-app, which cannot be read, so the exact leaking data structure and any cache/audit settings in code are unverified; the retention policy is known only from the container's own startup log lines.

Container logs are only available from 2026-11-23T16:47:04.30Z onward (pod started then) and nothing after the authorized window end 2026-11-23T16:47:41Z was retained in the read, so whether the current container later OOM-killed again is unknown.

No OOMKill/Evicted event exists in the event list for app-95; the OOM is evidenced only by the container's lastState, and no kubelet 'Killing' event text is available to confirm the kill time precisely beyond finishedAt 16:47:31Z.

No container-level memory or restart metric was available, so the actual working-set at the moment of the kill cannot be stated beyond the application's own '115.5 MB stored images' line at 90 images.
No change_history integration is available, so when Deployment orca or Secret orca-app was last modified before the pod started cannot be established.
next_steps: Open the orca application code in Secret orca-app (or its source repository) and cap the thumbnail cache and processed_images list, then redeploy and watch container memory working set.
Once Prometheus is reachable, chart container_memory_working_set_bytes against limits for pod orca-57fdcbf45f-djwxd over the incident window and watch for a repeat OOMKill (restart count increase).

Consider enabling a bounded audit sink (disk/object storage) so 'storing all processed images' no longer consumes pod memory, and add a startup log of per-image memory delta to correlate growth precisely.
If the pod keeps OOMKilling without code changes being allowed, raise limits.memory from 128Mi to a level above the observed retained footprint as a stop-gap while the leak is fixed.
